artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $V = \mathbb{F}_p^r$ be the $r$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_p$. For a finite subset (or multiset) $A \subseteq V$, define the set of subset sums
$$\Sigma(A) = \Big\{ \sum_{a \in B} a : B \subseteq A \Big\} \subseteq V,$$
with the convention that the empty subset sum is $0$. For each $j \in \{1, 2, \dots, r-1\}$, define
$$\lambda_j(A) = \max_{\substack{W \le V \\ \dim W = j}} |A \cap W|,$$
the largest number of elements of $A$ that can be captured by a $j$-dimensional subspace of $V$.

(a) Given positive real numbers $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_{r-1}$, determine a reasonable estimate, as a function of $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_{r-1}$, for the maximum possible size of a set $A \subseteq V$ which satisfies
$$\Sigma(A) \neq V \quad \text{and} \quad \lambda_j(A) \le \lambda_j \text{ for all } j = 1, \dots, r-1.$$

(b) In particular, prove or disprove the following: if $A \subseteq V$ satisfies $\lambda_j(A) < jp$ for every $j = 1, \dots, r-1$ and $\Sigma(A) \neq V$, then necessarily $|A| \le rp - 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return a specific resolution to this question on covering finite-dimensional vector spaces over $\mathbb{F}_p$ by subset sums under subspace-density constraints. Related work exists on sumsets in vector spaces over finite fields and on subset sums in such spaces, but no source clearly settles the proposed estimate or the specific bound $|A| \le rp - 2$ under the hypothesis $\lambda_j(A) < jp$. The status is therefore unclear.
